facts.text: Deadlock logging records deadlock events in Windows Event Log with AL code information and SQL Server deadlock report details.
Deadlock occurs when two or more transactions block each other from continuing by holding locked database resources.
Service account login requires View database state permission at database level and Alter any event session and View server state at instance level.
By default SQL Server uses ring_buffer target storing up to 5MB; event_file target provides greater storage for high volume situations.
Enable deadlock logging on Server instance using Administration Tool or Set-NAVServerConfiguration cmdlet with EnableDeadlockMonitoring parameter.
Deadlock events are recorded as warnings with event ID 705 and task category 33 in Server Admin channel log.
AL ObjectType, ObjectNumber, and ScopeName attributes may be empty if deadlock occurred on different Server instance.
